correctness.rationale: For a nonzero closed-range operator \(K\), the adjoint \(K^*\) is bounded below on \(R(K)\), so every surviving \(K\)-frame deletion yields a surviving projected ordinary frame, proving the one-sided inequality. Near \(K\)-Riesz equality follows from finite deletion to a projected Riesz basis. If all atoms lie in \(R(K)\), projected-frame lower bounds imply \(K\)-frame lower bounds, giving equivalence of legal deletions. The orthonormal-basis construction has exact excesses \(0\) and \(N-1\) for every \(N\ge2\).
